decision.summary: Inspection is done and the report went to the landlord. The landlord has now asked about an unapproved dog flap and a spare key after a lock change. I corrected our earlier "no issues" summary to the landlord, asked the tenant the open questions, and set a follow-up for 22 Feb.

answers.question: Where does this case stand and what is outstanding?
answers.answer: The inspection happened and the report was sent. Outstanding: the dog flap consent question, the lock change and spare key question, and the tenant removing the Bedroom 1 sticker marks. The ticket has not been closed.

answers.question: What is the next action, for whom, via which channel?
answers.answer: Reply to the landlord by email (sent) and ask the tenant by email (sent). Follow up on 22 Feb.

answers.question: Does anything need a human decision?
answers.answer: Not yet. If the tenant fitted the dog flap or changed the lock without consent, the remedy is a landlord decision, and a human is needed if that turns into a dispute. The sender name mismatch (Felix Clarke vs Oliver Bennett) is noted for checking.

args.body: Thank you for your email. Please note our earlier summary said no issues were found; the attached report actually records two points: a dog flap fitted in the back door/utility room, and sticker-type marks on the Bedroom 1 wall which the tenant is to remove and make good. We are checking with the tenant whether the dog flap was ever agreed and whether the front door lock was changed and who holds the spare key. We will not take any action on either until we have their answer, and will update you by 22 February. Could you also tell us whether you consented to the dog flap or lock change?
